title: Build the kiln row with four facing-correct furnaces and axis beams
goal: Reproduce the sealed 28-block Furnace Kiln Row on a fresh judged server: a stone floor, four furnaces that must verify facing west, east, north and south respectively, and oak_log beams that must verify on x and z axes. Directional blocks take their orientation from the placing bot's position, so the plan must compute a stand-point for every directional placement, and the verify loop must read back the scanned facing from the judger rather than trusting the placement call. Iterate placement, snapshot verification, and repair until the judger records block_hit_rate 1.0; a furnace with the right id but the wrong facing stays a miss.
resources: docker image itzg/minecraft-server:2024.6.1-java17 (Minecraft 1.19.2 vanilla; compose file assets/gc-363/docker-compose.yml)
docker image node:20.15.1 (Node 20 runtime for mineflayer bots and the judger's JS bridge)
process_expectations: The plan artifact lists, for each of the 9 directional blocks, the intended bot stand-point and look direction before execution
Facing verification actually ran: the run log shows per-coordinate scanned facing/axis compared against the blueprint after each placement batch
Wrong-orientation blocks are tracked by identity (coordinate, expected facing, scanned facing), broken, re-placed, and re-verified - the identities disappear from later verify output
Honest cost/failure logging: tokens.json spend entries and action_log.json intervals grow during the run, and every failed placement attempt is logged with its cause
